one_liner: x86-64 Linux syscall interposer: traps each syscall site once via Syscall User Dispatch, then rewrites it zpoline-style; exhaustive, near-zpoline steady state.
what_it_does: An LD_PRELOAD-able interposer (libbootstrap.so loads liblazypoline.so into a separate dlmopen namespace) that routes every system call of an unmodified x86-64 Linux process through one C++ function, syscall_emulate in lazypoline.cpp, which you edit to log, filter or emulate calls. Unlike zpoline, which rewrites only the syscall instructions it finds when the program loads, it also catches syscalls in code that is generated or mapped later (JITs, tcc output). There is no plugin API: you change the source and rebuild.
how_it_is_fast: Hybrid interposition: SUD (prctl PR_SET_SYSCALL_USER_DISPATCH, Linux 5.11+) delivers SIGSYS the first time a syscall site runs, and the handler overwrites that 2-byte `syscall` (0f 05) with `callq *%rax` (ff d0). Later executions jump into a nop sled mapped at virtual address 0 (the zpoline trampoline) and on to an assembly hook, with no signal and no kernel round trip for the redirect. A per-thread selector byte at %gs:0 is flipped to ALLOW while the interposer runs and back to BLOCK on return. xsave/xrstor of vector state (SAVE_VECTOR_REGS) is a compile-time option.
when_to_use: Tracing, sandboxing or emulating every syscall of an unmodified x86-64 Linux binary where ptrace or pure-SUD cost (one SIGSYS per call) is too high, e.g. syscall-heavy servers such as nginx or lighttpd, which the DSN 2024 artifact benchmarks

Programs that generate or load code at run time (JITs, tcc, dlopen'd plugins) where zpoline's load-time scan would miss sites; the artifact's exhaustiveness test shows zpoline missing getpid from tcc-generated code
Research or prototyping of syscall-level tools where you can edit and rebuild one C++ dispatch function
Kernels 5.11 or newer on hosts where you are allowed to set vm.mmap_min_addr=0
when_not_to_use: Security monitoring against a hostile application: the interposer shares the address space and its selector byte and is not isolated; the authors' Secpoline (github.com/lazypoline/secpoline, USENIX Security 2026) adds isolation and says it supersedes lazypoline
Non-x86-64 targets (the call *%rax trampoline is x86-specific; see svc-hook for ARM64) or kernels older than 5.11
Hosts where mapping page 0 is forbidden (vm.mmap_min_addr must be 0, a hardening regression), or apps that use the %gs base themselves

Applications that call unshare, use clone with CLONE_VM but without CLONE_THREAD or CLONE_VFORK, or need clone3: unshare and unsupported clone flags hit asserts, and clone3 is answered with -ENOSYS so glibc falls back to clone

Short-lived processes with many distinct syscall sites: each site pays one SIGSYS trap plus two mprotect calls before it is rewritten, and syscalls made before or during loading of the preload library are missed

integration.dependencies: CMake 3.16+, clang/clang++ (hard-coded in CMakeLists.txt), libpthread, libdl; glibc-specific sysdeps/ headers and SIGSETSIZE in util.h must match the running glibc
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 with clang (CMakeLists sets clang explicitly); built with -O3 -flto -march=native
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux 5.11+ only; tested on Ubuntu 20.04 and 22.04 (glibc 2.35); -march=native output is not portable to other CPUs
integration.thread_safety: Multi-threaded and multi-process programs are supported (per-thread state at %gs, rewrites under a spinlock, test cases in main.cpp cover threads, fork and signal delivery), but there is no formal statement
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: launched the same way as zpoline (LD_PRELOAD plus mmap_min_addr=0), but zpoline loads a separate hook library (LIBZPHOOK, __hook_init) while lazypoline is customised by editing syscall_emulate and rebuilding

gotchas: Harness flaw in the DSN artifact (github.com/lazypoline/benchmarks, bench/bench_micro.sh): the xstate-preserving 'lazypoline*' run comes straight after the 'SUD disable' step and never switches the microbenchmark back from mb_config_sud_disable.h, so the app turns SUD off before timing. That row therefore leaves out the kernel's SUD slow-path cost, and plot_micro.py also subtracts the SUD* overhead from the xstate segment, so the Figure 4 bar for the full configuration (SUD on, vector state saved) is understated by roughly the SUD* overhead.

The headline 'lazypoline' microbenchmark row uses config_rw_zpoline.h with SAVE_VECTOR_REGS 0, so the interposer does not preserve vector registers. The repository default is SAVE_VECTOR_REGS 1, the slower 'lazypoline*' row. The loop calls invalid syscall 500 (-ENOSYS) via a pre-written `callq *%rax`, so it measures steady-state hook cost on a near-empty kernel body, not the first-hit SIGSYS-and-rewrite path.

The default config.h has PRINT_SYSCALLS 1 (commit 'print syscalls by default', 2024-03-27), so an out-of-the-box build fprintf's every syscall to stderr; set it to 0 before measuring anything. asserts stay on in the -O3 build because NDEBUG is not defined.

rewrite_syscall_inst mprotects only the page holding the first byte of the 2-byte syscall (an instruction straddling a page boundary is not handled), makes the page write+exec without read while it patches, and then sets it to read+exec whatever it was before (JIT pages that need RWX need COMPAT_NONDEP_APP). The vDSO is assumed to be one page ('check whether your vdso is larger than a page'). Bugs fixed after the paper: red-zone clobbering on the signal-return trampoline (2025-04-21) and xsave across setup_new_thread (2025-01-12); the artifact pins src at aed8164, which predates both.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick lazypoline over zpoline when the target generates or loads code after startup and you need every syscall caught; zpoline rewrites everything at load time, has a hook-library API and no first-hit trap, so prefer it for static binaries. svc-hook is the ARM64 counterpart of zpoline, and the disassembler and assembler siblings solve unrelated problems.
verified_claims_summary: No numbers could be read: Table II and Figures 4-5 of the DSN 2024 paper are egress-blocked here (repository.tudelft.nl failed DNS, adriaanjacobs.github.io blocked), and neither repository prints results. The artifact's microbenchmark times 1e8 invocations of invalid syscall 500 with rdtsc on one pinned core, subtracts an empty-loop noise run, and reports the geometric mean of 10 runs as a ratio to a plain syscall loop for zpoline (with its rewritten-address check disabled by zpoline.patch), lazypoline, lazypoline with xstate preservation, SUD enabled without interposition, and pure SUD interposition. Everything is built with clang -O3 -flto -march=native (Ubuntu 22.04 apt clang) and run on a 48-core Xeon Gold 5318S, Linux 5.15.0-83, with hyperthreading off.
status_note: Research artifact with occasional maintenance (last code change 'redzone fix' 2025-04-21, README edit 2026-06-15, one closed build issue); MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor, but the authors point new users to Secpoline, which says it supersedes lazypoline. The published artifact's xstate microbenchmark row runs with SUD disabled, so its full-configuration overhead is understated.
